messages:
sec-alert-bot: EDR Alert: Suspicious outbound TLS connection from /usr/local/bin/updaterd (code-signed) on host maria-laptop. Suspicious domain: telemetry-update[.]svc-external[.]io. Action: quarantined file, network isolated host.

maria.ops: Whoa, that was my laptop. I clicked an update prompt earlier for 'System Helper'. No other apps open.

jonathan.eng: Thx for flagging. Can security confirm quarantine succeeded and whether the process persisted?

sec-alert-bot: Quarantine status: SUCCESS. PID 4127 killed during containment. Process command line: "/usr/local/bin/updaterd --auto". MD5: 9f2b7c1a4e3d6b8f4e2c3a5d7b9c0f1e. File signed by 'ACME Soft Inc' (valid signature chain).

jonathan.eng: Signed binary is odd. Could be maliciously signed or abused installer. Tess, can you pull the binary and share YARA fingerprints?

Tess.sece: On it. Maria, please keep laptop connected to power and the network in case we need live forensics; we'll keep it isolated via NAC. Also avoid reboots.

devon-it: I pushed an isolation policy to the switch — host is in 'containment' VLAN (no internet, only EDR/console comms). Confirmed.

jonathan.eng: Steps I'd like: 1) snapshot memory if possible; 2) dump /proc/4127/environ and /proc/4127/cmdline; 3) collect /usr/local/bin/updaterd; 4) list open sockets and connections.

Tess.sece: Running remote collection now via EDR agent. Commands executed: ```
sudo edrctl collect --pid 4127 --dump-mem /tmp/maria_mem.dmp
sudo edrctl fetch-file /usr/local/bin/updaterd --out /tmp/updaterd.bin
sudo edrctl netstat --pid 4127 > /tmp/4127_net.txt
```

sec-alert-bot: Collections complete. Memory dump uploaded to case-1897, file hash (updaterd.bin): sha256 = 3a7b9c2b5d1e4f6a8b9c0d2f3e4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2. YARA scan: flagged by ruleset: SUSP_UPDATER_2026.

maria.ops: Anything I should do on my side? No personal files are sensitive, but I do have SSH keys.

Tess.sece: Good Q. Immediate actions: rotate your user device certificate and any SSH keys used from this machine. We'll coordinate with IT. Avoid using the machine for auth until reimage.

devon-it: I'll generate new device cert and push. Maria: confirm which SSH keys you use from that laptop (default id_rsa/id_ed25519) and whether keys are in ssh-agent.

maria.ops: I use id_ed25519 and had the agent loaded this morning.

oncall-aaron: Noted. We'll assume potential key exposure. Devon, add Maria to the emergency key-rotation runbook and revoke old certs. Also create ticket to rotate any cloud KMS access tied to local credentials (if present).

jonathan.eng: Quick triage notes: Signed binary contacted telemetry-update domain with TLS SNI mismatch. Binary attempts to spawn child process /usr/local/bin/updaterd-helper. Helper not present on disk; observed in memory. Could be second-stage puller.

Tess.sece: Investigation next steps: 1) submit binary to vendor contact for signature verification; 2) check enterprise PKI to see if the signing cert maps to known vendor; 3) run static and dynamic analysis in isolated sandbox; 4) full disk scan for similar artifacts.

sec-alert-bot: Additional detection: EDR found a dropped file at /tmp/.sysconf-cache with suspicious crontab persistence attempt logged at 2026-06-18T09:12:03Z. File quarantined.

maria.ops: I did install a third-party app from a forum earlier this week, could that be related?

Tess.sece: Possibly. We'll enumerate recent installs. Please provide the install path or approximate time.

maria.ops: Thursday evening around 20:30 PT.

devon-it: Ticket created: IT-5482 (Device containment + reimage). Scheduling reimage tomorrow 09:00 PT if no blockers. Backup of user docs to secure share scheduled.

jonathan.eng: One more ask: Can we check if the binary used a valid timestamp in code-signing? Fake signing sometimes uses stolen certs but no timestamp authority. Tess?

Tess.sece: Checked: signature contains a timestamp token from tsa.acme-sigs.com; stamp appears valid. We're contacting vendor security to validate if their key was compromised.

oncall-aaron: Communication plan: 1) Tell impacted user (Maria) immediate do-not-use; 2) Notify infra and SRE for any anomalies in egress; 3) If vendor confirms compromise, prepare external disclosure template.

sec-alert-bot: Follow-up scan scheduled: full disk AV + heuristics tomorrow 02:00 UTC. EDR will run nightly elevated scan across all macOS/Linux endpoints for SUSP_UPDATER_2026 signature.

maria.ops: Thanks, team. I'll avoid the machine and let IT handle the reimage. Appreciate the quick action.

Tess.sece: Post-incident actions (to track): - Add rule to block telemetry-update domain at network perimeter. - Update onboarding guidance: warn about unsigned community installers. - Add check to device cert rotation runbook. - Review RBAC for who can install system-level daemons without IT approval.

jonathan.eng: I'll add an item to eng-security backlog: verify least-privilege for dev laptops (sudoers audit) and propose tightening.

devon-it: Reimage ticket updated to include manual SSH key purge, revoke sessions, and KMS access audit for Maria's user.

oncall-aaron: Closing note: Case-1897 opened. We'll reconvene in 24h with vendor update and sandbox results. :thumbsup:

maria.ops: Thanks everyone :)
